claim: Non-random functional connectivity during unconsciousness is a defining feature of supraspinal networks.
source: Non-random functional connectivity during unconsciousness is a defining feature of supraspinal networks.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific data from this study.

claim: Barry et al., 2014 used fMRI to reveal bilateral resting state functional connectivity within sensory-dominant and, separately, motor-dominant regions of the spinal cord.
source: Previously, Barry et al., 2014 used fMRI to reveal bilateral resting state functional connectivity within sensory-dominant and, separately, motor-dominant regions of the spinal cord.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Spontaneous functional connectivity links sensory- and motor-dominant regions of the spinal cord during unconsciousness.
source: Here, we record spike trains from large populations of spinal interneurons in vivo in rats and demonstrate that spontaneous functional connectivity also links sensory- and motor-dominant regions during unconsciousness.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The spatiotemporal patterns of connectivity could not be explained by latent afferent activity.
source: The spatiotemporal patterns of connectivity could not be explained by latent afferent activity or by populations of interconnected neurons spiking randomly.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data including nerve recordings and synthetic data comparisons.

claim: The spatiotemporal patterns of connectivity could not be explained by populations of interconnected neurons spiking randomly.
source: The spatiotemporal patterns of connectivity could not be explained by latent afferent activity or by populations of interconnected neurons spiking randomly.
evidence: This is supported by comparison with synthetic datasets generated by jittering spike times.

claim: Connection latencies compatible with mono- and disynaptic interactions were documented.
source: We also document connection latencies compatible with mono- and disynaptic interactions and putative excitatory and inhibitory connections.
evidence: This is supported by latency measurements shown in Figure 5e and Figure 7f.

claim: Putative excitatory and inhibitory connections were documented.
source: We also document connection latencies compatible with mono- and disynaptic interactions and putative excitatory and inhibitory connections.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 4c, 5d, and 7e.

claim: The observed activity is consistent with the hypothesis that salient, experience-dependent patterns of neural transmission introduced during behavior or by injury/disease are reactivated during unconsciousness.
source: The observed activity is consistent with the hypothesis that salient, experience-dependent patterns of neural transmission introduced during behavior or by injury/disease are reactivated during unconsciousness.
evidence: This is presented as a hypothesis consistent with the findings, not as directly tested.

claim: A spinal replay mechanism could shape circuit-level connectivity and ultimately behavior.
source: Such a spinal replay mechanism could shape circuit-level connectivity and ultimately behavior.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the potential functional significance of the findings.

claim: Synchronous neural activity across functionally and spatially distinct brain structures is a hallmark of sensorimotor integration, cognition, and behavior during periods of attentive wakefulness.
source: Synchronous neural activity across functionally and spatially distinct brain structures, that is, functional connectivity, is a hallmark of sensorimotor integration, cognition, and behavior during periods of attentive wakefulness.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Elucidation of brain networks intrinsically active during unconsciousness and inattentive wakefulness has led to a substantially more nuanced view of brain function.
source: Recent elucidation of brain networks intrinsically active during unconsciousness and inattentive wakefulness has led to a substantially more nuanced view of brain function (Demertzi et al., 2019; Fox et al., 2005; Greicius et al., 2003; Mashour and Hudetz, 2018; Raichle et al., 2001; Steriade et al., 1993; Wenzel et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Unconscious network activity spans multiple spatiotemporal scales.
source: Unconscious network activity spans multiple spatiotemporal scales and has known functions ranging from circuit-level synaptic stabilization (Puentes-Mestril and Aton, 2017; Tsodyks et al., 1999; Wei et al., 2016) to maintenance of ongoing physiological processes (Sanchez-Vives et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Unconscious network activity has known functions ranging from circuit-level synaptic stabilization to maintenance of ongoing physiological processes.
source: Unconscious network activity spans multiple spatiotemporal scales and has known functions ranging from circuit-level synaptic stabilization (Puentes-Mestril and Aton, 2017; Tsodyks et al., 1999; Wei et al., 2016) to maintenance of ongoing physiological processes (Sanchez-Vives et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: It has yet to be unequivocally confirmed whether spontaneous, non-random network activity during unconsciousness is a conserved feature of complex neural systems that generalizes to the spinal cord.
source: Although the finding of spontaneous, non-random network activity during unconsciousness appears to be robust across different functional regions of the brain, it has yet to be unequivocally confirmed whether this phenomenon is a conserved feature of complex neural systems that generalizes to the spinal cord.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Patterns of resting state functional connectivity in the spinal cord have only been preliminarily characterized.
source: Patterns of resting state functional connectivity in the spinal cord have only been preliminarily characterized (Barry et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2015; Conrad et al., 2018; Eippert et al., 2017; Kong et al., 2014; Tl et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The most reliable findings to date have been correlations between spontaneous BOLD signals in the left and right dorsal horns, and, separately, the left and right ventral horns.
source: The most reliable findings to date have been correlations between spontaneous BOLD signals in the left and right dorsal horns, and, separately, the left and right ventral horns (VHs) (Barry et al., 2014; Eippert et al., 2017; Kong et al., 2014; Tl et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Spontaneous connectivity between the dorsal horn and VH, between the intermediate gray and the VH, and within the VH itself has yet to be reliably delineated.
source: Spontaneous connectivity between the dorsal horn and VH, between the intermediate gray (IG) and the VH, and within the VH itself has yet to be reliably delineated.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: It is unknown whether network topologies evinced by spinal BOLD signals mirror those drawn from spike trains of individual neurons.
source: For example, it is unknown whether network topologies evinced by spinal BOLD signals mirror those drawn from spike trains of individual neurons.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge.

claim: BOLD signals are only indirectly linked to spiking activity.
source: Indeed, BOLD signals are only indirectly linked to spiking activity (Logothetis et al., 2001; Murayama et al., 2010; Vakorin et al., 2007), which is compounded by the relatively coarse spatiotemporal resolution of fMRI in the spinal cord.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: It is not readily apparent whether structured activity at the single-unit level actually persists in spinal networks during unconsciousness in the absence of evoked neural transmission.
source: It is also not readily apparent whether structured activity at the single-unit level actually persists in spinal networks during unconsciousness in the absence of evoked neural transmission.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Aggregate multi-unit and local field potential activity in the dorsal horn is broadly correlated with dorsal horn BOLD fluctuations during mechanical probing of the dermatome.
source: The most relevant evidence, which suggests that aggregate multi-unit and local field potential activity in the dorsal horn is broadly correlated with dorsal horn BOLD fluctuations, was made during mechanical probing of the dermatome (Tl et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The potential function(s) of resting state intraspinal connectivity are unknown.
source: The potential function(s) of resting state intraspinal connectivity are likewise unknown.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge.

claim: Resting state intraspinal connectivity may play a role in adaptive or maladaptive neural plasticity through a form of reactivation and synaptic stabilization during unconsciousness.
source: An intriguing possibility is that it plays a role in adaptive or maladaptive neural plasticity through a form of reactivation and synaptic stabilization during unconsciousness.
evidence: This is presented as a hypothesis drawn from supraspinal network function.

claim: This hypothesis is drawn from the function of supraspinal network activity during sleep.
source: This hypothesis is drawn from the function of supraspinal network activity during sleep (Abel et al., 2013; Puentes-Mestril and Aton, 2017; Wei et al., 2016) and is supported by the finding of altered patterns of BOLD-based intraspinal functional connectivity in conditions associated with maladaptive neural plasticity in spinal networks (Chen et al., 2015; Conrad et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Altered patterns of BOLD-based intraspinal functional connectivity are found in conditions associated with maladaptive neural plasticity in spinal networks.
source: This hypothesis is drawn from the function of supraspinal network activity during sleep (Abel et al., 2013; Puentes-Mestril and Aton, 2017; Wei et al., 2016) and is supported by the finding of altered patterns of BOLD-based intraspinal functional connectivity in conditions associated with maladaptive neural plasticity in spinal networks (Chen et al., 2015; Conrad et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: A necessary substrate for resting state connectivity to have a direct role in shaping neural plasticity would be the tandem presence of synchronous discharge amongst populations of individual units spanning multiple spatial and functional regions.
source: To have a direct role in shaping neural plasticity, however, a necessary substrate would be the tandem presence of synchronous discharge amongst populations of individual units spanning multiple spatial and functional regions.
evidence: This is a logical inference about what would be required for the hypothesized mechanism.

claim: Spontaneous functional connectivity between neurons in sensory-dominant and motor-dominant regions of the gray matter would be a precondition for functional network activity during unconsciousness.
source: Given the critical role played by the spinal cord in sensorimotor integration (broadly) and reflexes (specifically), we reasoned that spontaneous functional connectivity between neurons in sensory-dominant and motor-dominant regions of the gray matter would be a precondition for functional network activity during unconsciousness, regardless of its function.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the known role of the spinal cord.

claim: Experiments were performed in adult male Sprague–Dawley rats (N = 24).
source: Experiments were performed in adult male Sprague–Dawley rats (N = 24; weight), divided across two cohorts.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental subjects.

claim: Fifteen animals received urethane anesthesia (1.2 g/kg i.p.).
source: Fifteen animals received urethane anesthesia (1.2 g/kg i.p.).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental protocol.

claim: Nine animals received inhaled isoflurane anesthesia (2–4% in O2).
source: The remaining nine animals received inhaled isoflurane anesthesia (2–4% in O2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental protocol.

claim: The microelectrode array contained two shanks, each with 16 individual electrode contacts spaced uniformly at 100 μm intervals.
source: The microelectrode array contained two shanks, each with 16 individual electrode contacts spaced uniformly at 100 μm intervals (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is supported by both text description and Figure 1a.

claim: Electrode impedance ranged from ~1 to –4 kΩ per contact.
source: Electrode impedance ranged from ~1 to –4 kΩ per contact.
evidence: This is a direct statement of electrode properties.

claim: In total, approximately 860 well-isolated units were recorded across 13 urethane-anesthetized rats.
source: In total, we recorded from approximately 860 well-isolated units across 13 urethane-anesthetized rats, averaging 66 ± 8 units per trial (e.g., Figure 1a).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data collected, with reference to Figure 1a.

claim: An average of 66 ± 8 units per trial were recorded in urethane-anesthetized rats.
source: In total, we recorded from approximately 860 well-isolated units across 13 urethane-anesthetized rats, averaging 66 ± 8 units per trial (e.g., Figure 1a).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data collected.

claim: Approximately two units were discriminated per electrode across the array, with a range from 0 to ~5 units per electrode.
source: This per-animal average number of units corresponds to approximately two units discriminated per electrode across the array, with a range from 0 to ~5 units per electrode.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: Spontaneously active units can be observed throughout the dorsoventral extent of the sampled region.
source: Spontaneously active units can be observed throughout the dorsoventral extent of the sampled region.
evidence: This is supported by the raster plot in Figure 2a.

claim: Broadly distributed, robust discharge was a consistent feature of all animals.
source: Broadly distributed, robust discharge was a consistent feature of all animals.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the observed data across all animals.

claim: The mean number of spontaneously active units discriminated per gross anatomical region per trial in the urethane cohort was: sDH: 11 ± 3; dDH: 25 ± 3; IG: 16 ± 2; VH: 14 ± 2.
source: Across the urethane cohort, the mean number of spontaneously active units discriminated per gross anatomical region per trial was: sDH: 11 ± 3; dDH: 25 ± 3; IG: 16 ± 2; VH: 14 ± 2 (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data, with reference to Figure 2b.

claim: There was a significant main effect of region on connection number (F = 6.368, p=0.001).
source: We found a significant main effect of region on connection number (F = 6.368, p=0.001), which was driven by a significantly greater number of units in the dDH than the sDH or VH.
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: The significant main effect of region on connection number was driven by a significantly greater number of units in the dDH than the sDH or VH.
source: We found a significant main effect of region on connection number (F = 6.368, p=0.001), which was driven by a significantly greater number of units in the dDH than the sDH or VH.
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Across all animals and epochs in the urethane cohort, 4.2 ± 0.8% of unit pairs exhibited significantly correlated temporal discharge patterns.
source: Across all animals and epochs in the urethane cohort, 4.2 ± 0.8% of unit pairs exhibited significantly correlated temporal discharge patterns.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: Pairs of temporally correlated, spontaneously active units can be found at all sampled dorsoventral depths.
source: Qualitatively, it is evident from Figure 4 that pairs of temporally correlated, spontaneously active units can be found (a) at all sampled dorsoventral depths, (b) within each gross anatomical region, and (c) between all anatomical regions.
evidence: This is supported by the functional connectivity maps in Figure 4.

claim: Pairs of temporally correlated, spontaneously active units can be found within each gross anatomical region.
source: Qualitatively, it is evident from Figure 4 that pairs of temporally correlated, spontaneously active units can be found (a) at all sampled dorsoventral depths, (b) within each gross anatomical region, and (c) between all anatomical regions.
evidence: This is supported by the functional connectivity maps in Figure 4.

claim: Pairs of temporally correlated, spontaneously active units can be found between all anatomical regions.
source: Qualitatively, it is evident from Figure 4 that pairs of temporally correlated, spontaneously active units can be found (a) at all sampled dorsoventral depths, (b) within each gross anatomical region, and (c) between all anatomical regions.
evidence: This is supported by the functional connectivity maps in Figure 4.

claim: The proportion of significant connections within regions, at 68.9%, was significantly greater than the proportion of between-region connections, 31.1% (p<0.0001).
source: The proportion of significant connections within regions, at 68.9%, was significantly greater than the proportion of between-region connections, 31.1% (p<0.0001; Figure 5a).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results, with reference to Figure 5a.

claim: There was a main effect of anatomical region on the proportion of significant connections detected across all regions (F = 9.277, p<0.0001).
source: We also found a main effect of anatomical region on the proportion of significant connections detected across all regions (F = 9.277, p<0.0001; Figure 5a, Supplementary file 1, tab 1b; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Pairs of units within the dDH, IG, and VH accounted for the highest overall proportion of connections (24.9 ± 3.6, 17.3 ± 3.7, and 17.4 ± 3.7%, respectively).
source: This effect was driven (a) by pairs of units within the dDH, IG, and VH, which accounted for the highest overall proportion of connections (24.9 ± 3.6, 17.3 ± 3.7, and 17.4 ± 3.7%, respectively), and (b) by sDH-IG and sDH-VH pairs, which exhibited the lowest proportion of significant connections (1.5% and 1.2%, respectively).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: sDH-IG and sDH-VH pairs exhibited the lowest proportion of significant connections (1.5% and 1.2%, respectively).
source: This effect was driven (a) by pairs of units within the dDH, IG, and VH, which accounted for the highest overall proportion of connections (24.9 ± 3.6, 17.3 ± 3.7, and 17.4 ± 3.7%, respectively), and (b) by sDH-IG and sDH-VH pairs, which exhibited the lowest proportion of significant connections (1.5% and 1.2%, respectively).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: The proportion of significant connections was inversely related to connection distance.
source: Predictably, the proportion of significant connections was inversely related to connection distance.
evidence: This is an inference from the data pattern observed.

claim: Nodes in the dDH were classified as belonging to the most connected group in a greater proportion of trials (35.4 ± 4.6%) than nodes in the sDH (14.1 ± 4.3%), IG (27.4 ± 4.4%), or VH (23.0 ± 3.9%).
source: Nodes in the dDH were classified as belonging to the most connected group in a greater proportion of trials (35.4 ± 4.6%) than nodes in the sDH (14.1 ± 4.3%), IG (27.4 ± 4.4%), or VH (23.0 ± 3.9%), driving an overall main effect of anatomical region on the distribution of most connected nodes (F = 4.333, p=0.009; Figure 5b, Supplementary file 1, tab 1c).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: There was an overall main effect of anatomical region on the distribution of most connected nodes (F = 4.333, p=0.009).
source: Nodes in the dDH were classified as belonging to the most connected group in a greater proportion of trials (35.4 ± 4.6%) than nodes in the sDH (14.1 ± 4.3%), IG (27.4 ± 4.4%), or VH (23.0 ± 3.9%), driving an overall main effect of anatomical region on the distribution of most connected nodes (F = 4.333, p=0.009; Figure 5b, Supplementary file 1, tab 1c).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Connections within the dDH, within the IG, and within the VH contained the highest proportion of putative inhibitory connections (22.7 ± 5.3%, 24.1 ± 7.3%, and 37.8 ± 9.0%, respectively).
source: We found that connections within the dDH, within the IG, and within the VH contained the highest proportion of putative inhibitory connections (22.7 ± 5.3%, 24.1 ± 7.3%, and 37.8 ± 9.0%, respectively), with the dDH containing the highest proportion of excitatory connections (25.9 ± 3.7%).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: The dDH contained the highest proportion of excitatory connections (25.9 ± 3.7%).
source: We found that connections within the dDH, within the IG, and within the VH contained the highest proportion of putative inhibitory connections (22.7 ± 5.3%, 24.1 ± 7.3%, and 37.8 ± 9.0%, respectively), with the dDH containing the highest proportion of excitatory connections (25.9 ± 3.7%).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: Only the dDH displayed an approximately balanced proportion of excitation and inhibition.
source: Interestingly, only the dDH displayed an approximately balanced proportion of excitation and inhibition – that is, nearly the same proportion of the overall number of putative excitatory connections as overall putative inhibitory connections.
evidence: This is an observation from the data analysis.

claim: Mean excitatory latency was significantly longer than the mean inhibitory latency, at 6.4 ± 0.6 ms vs. 2.7 ± 0.4 ms (p=0.0003).
source: Mean excitatory latency was significantly longer than the mean inhibitory latency, at 6.4 ± 0.6 ms vs. 2.7 ± 0.4 ms (p=0.0003), with both categories including latencies consistent with putative mono-, di-, and polysynaptic pathways.
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Both excitatory and inhibitory connections include latencies consistent with putative mono-, di-, and polysynaptic pathways.
source: Mean excitatory latency was significantly longer than the mean inhibitory latency, at 6.4 ± 0.6 ms vs. 2.7 ± 0.4 ms (p=0.0003), with both categories including latencies consistent with putative mono-, di-, and polysynaptic pathways.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the latency data shown in Figure 5e.

claim: A subset of both excitatory and inhibitory connections have latencies between 0 and 1 ms.
source: Interestingly, we find a subset of both excitatory and inhibitory connections with latencies between 0 and 1 ms.
evidence: This is an observation from the latency distribution data.

claim: The most likely interpretation for coincidentally firing unit pairs with latencies between 0 and 1 ms would be a shared presynaptic input.
source: While some of these connections could indeed be monosynaptic and the lower-than-expected delay merely related to binning spikes, the most likely interpretation for coincidentally firing unit pairs would be a shared presynaptic input.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the very short latency connections.

claim: Urethane profoundly depresses spontaneous discharge in the dorsal root ganglia.
source: Although urethane profoundly depresses spontaneous discharge in the dorsal root ganglia, it exerts less of a depressive effect on cells deep in the gray matter (i.e., the IG and VH) (Daló and Hackman, 2013; Hara and Harris, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Urethane exerts less of a depressive effect on cells deep in the gray matter (i.e., the IG and VH).
source: Although urethane profoundly depresses spontaneous discharge in the dorsal root ganglia, it exerts less of a depressive effect on cells deep in the gray matter (i.e., the IG and VH) (Daló and Hackman, 2013; Hara and Harris, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Isoflurane is a more potent depressant of spinal motor activity than urethane.
source: Isoflurane is a more potent depressant of spinal motor activity than urethane, with an overall gradient of depression that increases from the dorsal horn to the VH (Kim et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Isoflurane has an overall gradient of depression that increases from the dorsal horn to the VH.
source: Isoflurane is a more potent depressant of spinal motor activity than urethane, with an overall gradient of depression that increases from the dorsal horn to the VH (Kim et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Nociceptive pathways in the sDH remain largely uninhibited by isoflurane.
source: For example, while nociceptive pathways in the sDH remain largely uninhibited by isoflurane, premotor interneurons and motoneurons in the VH are markedly depressed (Grasshoff and Antkowiak, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Premotor interneurons and motoneurons in the VH are markedly depressed by isoflurane.
source: For example, while nociceptive pathways in the sDH remain largely uninhibited by isoflurane, premotor interneurons and motoneurons in the VH are markedly depressed (Grasshoff and Antkowiak, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Mean intraspinal resting motor threshold confirmed the greater depression of VH cells by isoflurane than urethane (isoflurane threshold: 20.4 μA; urethane threshold 14.0 μA).
source: Mean intraspinal resting motor threshold confirmed the greater depression of VH cells by isoflurane than urethane (isoflurane threshold: 20.4 μA; urethane threshold 14.0 μA).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental measurements.

claim: In total, 484 well-isolated units were recorded across the nine isoflurane-anesthetized rats.
source: In total, we recorded from 484 well-isolated units across the nine rats, translating to ~51 ± 2 units per trial.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data collected.

claim: Approximately 51 ± 2 units per trial were recorded in isoflurane-anesthetized rats.
source: In total, we recorded from 484 well-isolated units across the nine rats, translating to ~51 ± 2 units per trial.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data collected.

claim: The mean number of units recorded per trial did not differ between the urethane and the isoflurane cohorts (p=0.0718).
source: The mean number of units recorded per trial did not differ between the urethane and the isoflurane cohorts (p=0.0718).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Spontaneously active units were observed throughout the dorsoventral extent of the sampled region in all isoflurane-anesthetized animals, including the IG and VH.
source: Surprisingly, spontaneously active units were observed throughout the dorsoventral extent of the sampled region in all animals, including the IG and VH.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the observed data.

claim: The mean numbers of units per region in the isoflurane cohort are: sDH: 9 ± 2, dDH: 20 ± 3, IG: 12 ± 1, VH: 13 ± 1.
source: The mean numbers of units per region are as follows: sDH: 9 ± 2, dDH: 20 ± 3, IG: 12 ± 1, VH: 13 ± 1 (main effect of region: F = 6.650, p=0.001; Figure 6b, Supplementary file 1, tab 1d).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: There was a main effect of region on the number of units in the isoflurane cohort (F = 6.650, p=0.001).
source: The mean numbers of units per region are as follows: sDH: 9 ± 2, dDH: 20 ± 3, IG: 12 ± 1, VH: 13 ± 1 (main effect of region: F = 6.650, p=0.001; Figure 6b, Supplementary file 1, tab 1d).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: In the isoflurane cohort, the proportion of connections within regions (66.4%) was significantly greater than across regions (33.6%) (p=0.005).
source: Similar to the urethane cohort, we observed a significantly greater proportion of connections within regions (66.4%) than across regions (33.6%) (p=0.005), and an overall main effect of anatomical region (e.g., sDH-sDH, sDH-dDH) on the proportion of significant connections (F = 6.517, p<0.0001; Supplementary file 1, tab 1e).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: There was an overall main effect of anatomical region on the proportion of significant connections in the isoflurane cohort (F = 6.517, p<0.0001).
source: Similar to the urethane cohort, we observed a significantly greater proportion of connections within regions (66.4%) than across regions (33.6%) (p=0.005), and an overall main effect of anatomical region (e.g., sDH-sDH, sDH-dDH) on the proportion of significant connections (F = 6.517, p<0.0001; Supplementary file 1, tab 1e).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: There was no systematic difference in the proportion of significant connections per region across the urethane and isoflurane cohorts (anesthetic by region interaction: F = 0.369, p=0.949; main effect of anesthetic: F = 0.631, p=0.436).
source: Interestingly, despite the different mechanisms of action and depressive profiles of the two anesthetics, we found no systematic difference in the proportion of significant connections per region across the urethane and isoflurane cohorts (anesthetic by region interaction: F = 0.369, p=0.949; main effect of anesthetic: F = 0.631, p=0.436); rather, all were within 1.8% of one another on average (range, 4–6%, Figure 7b).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: The proportion of significant connections per region were all within 1.8% of one another on average across the urethane and isoflurane cohorts (range, 4–6%).
source: Interestingly, despite the different mechanisms of action and depressive profiles of the two anesthetics, we found no systematic difference in the proportion of significant connections per region across the urethane and isoflurane cohorts (anesthetic by region interaction: F = 0.369, p=0.949; main effect of anesthetic: F = 0.631, p=0.436); rather, all were within 1.8% of one another on average (range, 4–6%, Figure 7b).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: In the isoflurane cohort, the largest proportion of most connected nodes was found in the dDH (34.2%), the lowest in the sDH (13.2%), with 22.6% in the IG and 30.0% in the VH.
source: The distribution of most connected nodes in the isoflurane cohort also mirrored that of the urethane cohort. Specifically, the largest proportion of most connected nodes was found in the dDH (34.2%), the lowest in the sDH (13.2%), with 22.6% in the IG and 30.0% in the VH.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: There was a significant main effect of region on most connected node in the isoflurane cohort (F = 4.935, p=0.006).
source: There was a significant main effect of region on most connected node (F = 4.935, p=0.006; Supplementary file 1, tab 1f; Figure 7c, d).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: There was no main effect of anesthetic agent nor an interaction of drug by region for the proportion of excitatory links in each region.
source: There was no main effect of anesthetic agent nor an interaction of drug by region for either the proportion of excitatory or inhibitory links in each region (excitatory: region: F = 13.981, p=0.000; region*drug: F = 0.348, p=0.819; drug: F = 0.030, p=0.865, Supplementary file 1, tab 1g; inhibitory: region: F = 19.403; p=0.000; region*drug: F = 0.231, p=0.794; drug: F = 0.611, p=0.444, Supplementary file 1, tab 1h).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: There was no main effect of anesthetic agent nor an interaction of drug by region for the proportion of inhibitory links in each region.
source: There was no main effect of anesthetic agent nor an interaction of drug by region for either the proportion of excitatory or inhibitory links in each region (excitatory: region: F = 13.981, p=0.000; region*drug: F = 0.348, p=0.819; drug: F = 0.030, p=0.865, Supplementary file 1, tab 1g; inhibitory: region: F = 19.403; p=0.000; region*drug: F = 0.231, p=0.794; drug: F = 0.611, p=0.444, Supplementary file 1, tab 1h).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: The mean latency of excitatory connections did not change from the urethane to the isoflurane cohorts (6.4 ± 0.5 vs. 6.7 ± 1 ms, p=0.8188).
source: The mean latency of excitatory and inhibitory connections also did not change from the urethane to the isoflurane cohorts (excitatory: 6.4 ± 0.5 vs. 6.7 ± 1 ms, p=0.8188; inhibitory: 2.6 ± 0.4 vs. 3.1 ± 0.6 ms, p=0.5389).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: The mean latency of inhibitory connections did not change from the urethane to the isoflurane cohorts (2.6 ± 0.4 vs. 3.1 ± 0.6 ms, p=0.5389).
source: The mean latency of excitatory and inhibitory connections also did not change from the urethane to the isoflurane cohorts (excitatory: 6.4 ± 0.5 vs. 6.7 ± 1 ms, p=0.8188; inhibitory: 2.6 ± 0.4 vs. 3.1 ± 0.6 ms, p=0.5389).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Within the isoflurane cohort, inhibitory latencies were significantly shorter than excitatory latencies (p=0.017).
source: Within the isoflurane cohort, inhibitory latencies were significantly shorter than excitatory latencies (p=0.017; Figure 7f), which was also reflected when pooling data across both cohorts (i.e., inhibitory latencies were significantly shorter than excitatory latencies on average at 2.9 vs. 6.5 ms, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: When pooling data across both cohorts, inhibitory latencies were significantly shorter than excitatory latencies on average at 2.9 vs. 6.5 ms (p<0.0001).
source: Within the isoflurane cohort, inhibitory latencies were significantly shorter than excitatory latencies (p=0.017; Figure 7f), which was also reflected when pooling data across both cohorts (i.e., inhibitory latencies were significantly shorter than excitatory latencies on average at 2.9 vs. 6.5 ms, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: The mean proportion of significantly correlated unit pairs in the synthetic datasets was significantly lower than that observed experimentally in the urethane cohort (short-latency synthetic: 2.7 ± 0.4%, long-latency synthetic: 2.6 ± 0.5%, experimentally observed: 4.2 ± 0.8%, p=0.0053).
source: Across animals, we find that the mean proportion of significantly correlated unit pairs in the synthetic datasets was significantly lower than that observed experimentally (urethane: short-latency synthetic: 2.7 ± 0.4%, long-latency synthetic: 2.6 ± 0.5%, experimentally observed: 4.2 ± 0.8%, p=0.0053; isoflurane: short-latency synthetic: 2.7 ± 1.1%, long-latency synthetic: 2.6 ± 0.5%, experimentally observed, 3.9 ± 1.3, p=0.0033).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results comparing observed to synthetic data.

claim: The mean proportion of significantly correlated unit pairs in the synthetic datasets was significantly lower than that observed experimentally in the isoflurane cohort (short-latency synthetic: 2.7 ± 1.1%, long-latency synthetic: 2.6 ± 0.5%, experimentally observed: 3.9 ± 1.3, p=0.0033).
source: Across animals, we find that the mean proportion of significantly correlated unit pairs in the synthetic datasets was significantly lower than that observed experimentally (urethane: short-latency synthetic: 2.7 ± 0.4%, long-latency synthetic: 2.6 ± 0.5%, experimentally observed: 4.2 ± 0.8%, p=0.0053; isoflurane: short-latency synthetic: 2.7 ± 1.1%, long-latency synthetic: 2.6 ± 0.5%, experimentally observed, 3.9 ± 1.3, p=0.0033).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results comparing observed to synthetic data.

claim: On a per-animal level, the proportion of significant connections in the observed data always exceeded its synthetic counterpart.
source: On a per-animal level, we find that the proportion of significant connections in the observed data always exceeded its synthetic counterpart; that is, in no animals did we detect only as few (or fewer) significant connections than would be expected at random when controlling for the uniqueness of each animal's own data.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: The overall degree of temporal synchrony was highly unlikely to be observed at random.
source: These findings indicate that the overall degree of temporal synchrony was highly unlikely to be observed at random.
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison with synthetic data.

claim: There was an overall main effect of anatomical region on connectivity patterns between the bootstrapped synthetic data and the observed data in the urethane cohort (F = 10.571, p<0.0001).
source: We found an overall main effect of anatomical region on connectivity patterns between the bootstrapped synthetic data and the observed data (urethane: F = 10.571, p<0.0001, Figure 8b, Supplementary file 1, tab 1i; isoflurane: F = 7.251, p=0.001, Supplementary file 1, tab 1j) and, notably, a significant interaction of region by cohort (i.e., real or synthetic urethane data; F = 16.168; p<0.0001 Supplementary file 1, tab 1i; isoflurane: F = 11.561, p<0.0001, Supplementary file 1, tab 1j).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: There was an overall main effect of anatomical region on connectivity patterns between the bootstrapped synthetic data and the observed data in the isoflurane cohort (F = 7.251, p=0.001).
source: We found an overall main effect of anatomical region on connectivity patterns between the bootstrapped synthetic data and the observed data (urethane: F = 10.571, p<0.0001, Figure 8b, Supplementary file 1, tab 1i; isoflurane: F = 7.251, p=0.001, Supplementary file 1, tab 1j) and, notably, a significant interaction of region by cohort (i.e., real or synthetic urethane data; F = 16.168; p<0.0001 Supplementary file 1, tab 1i; isoflurane: F = 11.561, p<0.0001, Supplementary file 1, tab 1j).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: There was a significant interaction of region by cohort (real or synthetic) in the urethane data (F = 16.168; p<0.0001).
source: We found an overall main effect of anatomical region on connectivity patterns between the bootstrapped synthetic data and the observed data (urethane: F = 10.571, p<0.0001, Figure 8b, Supplementary file 1, tab 1i; isoflurane: F = 7.251, p=0.001, Supplementary file 1, tab 1j) and, notably, a significant interaction of region by cohort (i.e., real or synthetic urethane data; F = 16.168; p<0.0001 Supplementary file 1, tab 1i; isoflurane: F = 11.561, p<0.0001, Supplementary file 1, tab 1j).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: There was a significant interaction of region by cohort (real or synthetic) in the isoflurane data (F = 11.561, p<0.0001).
source: We found an overall main effect of anatomical region on connectivity patterns between the bootstrapped synthetic data and the observed data (urethane: F = 10.571, p<0.0001, Figure 8b, Supplementary file 1, tab 1i; isoflurane: F = 7.251, p=0.001, Supplementary file 1, tab 1j) and, notably, a significant interaction of region by cohort (i.e., real or synthetic urethane data; F = 16.168; p<0.0001 Supplementary file 1, tab 1i; isoflurane: F = 11.561, p<0.0001, Supplementary file 1, tab 1j).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Post-hoc testing revealed a lower proportion of significant sDH-dDH, sDH-IG, sDH-VH, dDH-IG, and dDH-VH connections in the real compared to the synthetic dataset.
source: Post-hoc testing across regions revealed a lower proportion of significant sDH-dDH, sDH-IG, sDH-VH, dDH-IG, and dDH-VH connections in the real compared to the synthetic dataset and a significantly greater proportion of dDH-dDH, IG-IG, and VH-VH connections in the observed compared to the synthetic dataset (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: Post-hoc testing revealed a significantly greater proportion of dDH-dDH, IG-IG, and VH-VH connections in the observed compared to the synthetic dataset.
source: Post-hoc testing across regions revealed a lower proportion of significant sDH-dDH, sDH-IG, sDH-VH, dDH-IG, and dDH-VH connections in the real compared to the synthetic dataset and a significantly greater proportion of dDH-dDH, IG-IG, and VH-VH connections in the observed compared to the synthetic dataset (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: There was a significantly greater proportion of within-region connections in the observed dataset than the synthetic dataset (68.9 vs. 26.3%, p<0.0001).
source: Overall, we found a significantly greater proportion of within-region connections in the observed dataset than the synthetic dataset (68.9 vs. 26.3%, p<0.0001) and a significantly lower proportion of between-region connections in the observed dataset compared to the synthetic dataset (31.1 vs. 73.7%, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: There was a significantly lower proportion of between-region connections in the observed dataset compared to the synthetic dataset (31.1 vs. 73.7%, p<0.0001).
source: Overall, we found a significantly greater proportion of within-region connections in the observed dataset than the synthetic dataset (68.9 vs. 26.3%, p<0.0001) and a significantly lower proportion of between-region connections in the observed dataset compared to the synthetic dataset (31.1 vs. 73.7%, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: No spontaneous action potential discharge was evident in the sciatic nerve during periods without sensory stimulation.
source: In the anesthetized, unblocked state, action potential discharge was not evident during periods without sensory stimulation (Figure 9b).
evidence: This is supported by the ENG recordings shown in Figure 9b.

claim: Overall ENG amplitude was negligible during periods without sensory stimulation, and its standard deviation remained constant.
source: Overall ENG amplitude was also negligible during these periods, and its standard deviation remained constant.
evidence: This is supported by the ENG recordings.

claim: No persistent or spontaneously arising action potential discharge is evident during epochs between sensory stimulation.
source: Note that no persistent or spontaneously arising action potential discharge is evident during epochs between sensory stimulation; that is, the nerve returns to quiescence.
evidence: This is supported by the ENG recordings shown in Figure 9c and 9d.

claim: Bursts of multi-unit ENG had an average peak amplitude 16.7× (±0.82 sem) greater than the average amplitude of spontaneous baseline ENG (N = 51 pairs).
source: Across modalities of induced sensory transmission, bursts of multi-unit ENG had an average peak amplitude 16.7× (±0.82 sem) greater than the average amplitude of spontaneous baseline ENG (N = 51 pairs).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: The average ENG amplitude across each period of sensory stimulation was 3.09× (±0.17 sem) greater than the sum of the spontaneous baseline ENG amplitude and its standard deviation.
source: The average ENG amplitude across each period of sensory stimulation (not the average peak amplitude, as previously reported) was 3.09× (±0.17 sem) greater than the sum of the spontaneous baseline ENG amplitude and its standard deviation.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: The spontaneous baseline ENG is indistinguishable pre- and post-lidocaine nerve block.
source: Qualitatively, it is evident that the spontaneous baseline ENG is indistinguishable pre- and post-block (Figure 9b vs. Figure 9e).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of ENG recordings in Figure 9b and 9e.

claim: The average spontaneous baseline ENG before the block is indistinguishable from that during the block.
source: This similarity is represented quantitatively in Figure 9f, which shows that the average spontaneous baseline ENG before the block (black bar) is indistinguishable from that during the block (gray bar).
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative data shown in Figure 9f.

claim: The spinal cord possesses intrinsic networks that maintain functionality during unconsciousness and in the absence of evoked neural transmission.
source: We interpret our findings as supporting the emerging view that the spinal cord possesses intrinsic networks that maintain functionality during unconsciousness and in the absence of evoked neural transmission (Barry et al., 2014; Eippert and Tracey, 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In intrinsic supraspinal networks, functional neural transmission during unconsciousness involves patterned activity within local and regional circuits as well as communication between functionally and spatially distributed neural structures.
source: In intrinsic surpraspinal networks, functional neural transmission during unconsciousness involves patterned activity within local and regional circuits as well as communication between functionally and spatially distributed neural structures (Demertzi et al., 2019; Fox et al., 2005; Greicius et al., 2003; Mashour and Hudetz, 2018; Raichle et al., 2001; Steriade et al., 1993; Wenzel et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: More than 20% of all significant connections were between the sDH or dDH and the IG or VH.
source: Remarkably, we found that >20% of all significant connections were between the sDH or dDH and the IG or VH (e.g., Figure 5a).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: This is the first demonstration of single-neuron-level spontaneous functional connectivity between sensory and motor regions of the spinal gray matter during unconsciousness.
source: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first such demonstration of single-neuron-level spontaneous functional connectivity between sensory and motor regions of the spinal gray matter during unconsciousness.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: Spontaneous synchronous discharge of spinal neurons during unconsciousness is not confined to local, sensory-dominant circuits in the dorsal horn; rather, it spans spatially and functionally distinct regions of the spinal gray matter.
source: From these findings, we can conclude that spontaneous synchronous discharge of spinal neurons during unconsciousness is not confined to local, sensory-dominant circuits in the dorsal horn; rather, it spans spatially and functionally distinct regions of the spinal gray matter, reflecting the integrative nature of spinal neural transmission during periods of wakeful behavior.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data.

claim: The primary source of proprioceptive input to the IG and VH would be proprioceptive muscle and joint afferents, in particular the 1a, 1b, and group II fibers.
source: The primary source of such input would be proprioceptive muscle and joint afferents, in particular the 1a, 1b, and group II fibers.
evidence: This is stated as established anatomical knowledge.

claim: In the experimental preparation, muscle length was held constant.
source: While 1a afferents indeed synapse directly onto motoneurons, in our preparation muscle length was held constant.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental conditions.

claim: Activity in 1b and Group II afferents would be negligible in the experimental preparation, as muscles were not developing tension and were held in a neutral, unstrained position.
source: Activity in 1b and Group II afferents would likewise be negligible in our preparation, as muscles were not developing tension and were held in a neutral, unstrained position.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental conditions.

claim: Physical deafferentation could have paradoxically increased discharge in the residual dorsal roots, second-order neurons, or local dorsal horn neurons.
source: Although physical deafferentation would have wholly eliminated natural sensory afferent activity, it could have paradoxically increased discharge in the residual dorsal roots, second-order neurons, or local dorsal horn neurons (Eschenfelder et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The spatiotemporal patterns of connectivity are remarkably consistent across the two anesthetic agents.
source: In fact, we find the spatiotemporal patterns of connectivity to be remarkably consistent across the two anesthetic agents.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the comparison between urethane and isoflurane cohorts.

claim: An average of 105% more pairs of functionally connected units were found across rats in the observed compared to the synthetic datasets.
source: We developed a series of large synthetic datasets to address these questions, finding an average of 105% more pairs of functionally connected units across rats in the observed compared to the synthetic datasets.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the comparison between observed and synthetic data.

claim: The observed proportion of functionally connected units was unlikely to have occurred by chance.
source: This comparison is the most direct application of our synthetic datasets, and our findings indicate that the observed proportion of functionally connected units was unlikely to have occurred by chance.
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison with synthetic data.

claim: The spinal cord possesses intrinsic networks active during unconsciousness, which could be involved in multimodal neural processing.
source: It also reinforces the view that the spinal cord indeed possesses intrinsic networks active during unconsciousness, which could be involved in multimodal neural processing.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Significantly greater within-region connectivity than between-region connectivity was found overall (~70 vs. ~30%).
source: Indeed, we found significantly greater within-region connectivity than between-region connectivity overall (~70 vs. ~30%), opposite our prediction.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis results.

claim: The sDH is a particularly challenging region to study in vivo using implanted microelectrode arrays.
source: Indeed, its proximity to the electrode insertion site increases the likelihood of tissue damage, which is compounded by the small size and fragility of the cells it contains (e.g., in the substantia gelatinosa).
evidence: This is stated as a known technical challenge.

claim: The sDH contains a preponderance of between-region circuits dedicated to transmission of nociceptive neural activity from the periphery.
source: The sDH also contains a preponderance of between-region circuits dedicated to transmission of nociceptive neural activity from the periphery, but nociception was not a component of our protocol.
evidence: This is stated as established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Approximately one in every five observed connections spanned sensory-dominant and motor-dominant regions.
source: Despite all of the above considerations, however, it is worth reiterating that approximately one in every five observed connections spanned sensory-dominant and motor-dominant regions.
evidence: This is a restatement of a key finding from the data.

claim: During sleep, specific patterns of hippocampal and cortical activation emerge that mirror those experienced during wakefulness.
source: During sleep, for example, specific patterns of hippocampal and cortical activation emerge that mirror those experienced during wakefulness (Puentes-Mestril and Aton, 2017; Wei et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Persistence of specific patterns of neural activation during sleep is believed to be integral to memory encoding and consolidation.
source: Persistence of these patterns is believed to be integral to memory encoding and consolidation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Structured spontaneous activity during unconsciousness is a fundamental property of complex neural systems and is not confined to supraspinal networks.
source: Nevertheless, our results suggest that structured spontaneous activity during unconsciousness is a fundamental property of complex neural systems and is not confined to supraspinal networks.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings.
